name: Green Ridge State Forest Free Primitive Campsites

management_agency.name: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Forest Service

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - Self-registration at Forest Headquarters required (zero fee)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Primitive camping allowed at designated numbered campsites distributed across 47,000 acres of state forest land. Registration slip must be attached to site post.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6-8 inches deep in shale/loam soil, 200 feet from Potomac River and streams. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace. No trash receptacles on site.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only within the forest.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires allowed in existing stone fire rings. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Maryland DNR Forest Service burn bans during dry spring/autumn.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved gravel and dirt forest service roads (Mertens Avenue / Kocienda Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Winding gravel forest roads over mountain ridges with steep grades, ruts, and washboards.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible on main gravel forest roads in dry weather; high clearance recommended for remote side spurs)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 3-4 bars 5G/LTE (20-50 Mbps download on ridge sites)
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low on ridge tops; Moderate down along Potomac River bottomlands

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-70°F, blooming mountain laurel, spring rainstorms, muddy side tracks.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot 80-88°F, shaded oak canopy, high insect activity.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Spectacular Appalachian autumn foliage (55-70°F daytime, 40-50°F nights), dry roads.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cool 30-45°F, freezing nights, occasional snow dustings.

dangers_and_hazards: Copperheads and Timber Rattlesnakes active in warm months
Black Bears present in Western Maryland - store food securely

common_human_made_sounds: Distant I-68 highway hum from high northern ridge points (3 miles away)

human_demographics_and_culture: C&O Canal cyclists, Appalachian backpackers, hunters during autumn, and digital nomads.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Shawnee and Susquehannock indigenous traditions honor the Potomac River gorge and Green Ridge mountains as sacred hunting and spirit grounds.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Appalachian shale ridge energy, serene forest silence, elevated solar panel exposure.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding ridge trails, scenic overlooks of Potomac River bends

public_reviews_summary: Outstanding free primitive camping system in Western Maryland. Easy self-registration, clean sites, and fast 5G cell internet on ridge sites.
other_data: Bortle Class 3 night sky. Free registration at forest HQ required.

name: Savage River State Forest Dispersed Primitive Camping

management_agency.name: Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) - Forest Service

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - Maryland DNR State Forest Primitive Dispersed Camping (zero fee outside developed campsites)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted at designated forest pullouts along Savage River Road and Westernport Road. Camp 100ft minimum from water.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Dig cat-hole 6-8 inches deep in soil 200 feet from Savage River. Pack out hygiene items.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Dead and down wood gathering permitted on site.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock rings only. Fully douse with water before vacating.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Spring and fall forest fire warnings.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved county road to gravel State Forest Service roads
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Graded gravel forest roads, flat pullout turnouts.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Accessible by standard 2WD low clearance passenger cars.

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate in deep Savage River gorges

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 45-62°F, blooming mountain laurel, cold trout streams.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 70-82°F, cool mountain escape from Baltimore/DC summer heat.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: 20-38°F, crisp mountain snow, icy river banks.

dangers_and_hazards: High river currents during spring rain runoff
Black bears in Garrett County (store food securely)

acoustic_environment.quietness_rating: 9/10 - Rushing trout stream and mountain forest breeze

human_demographics_and_culture: Allegheny mountain locals, trout anglers, Maryland nomads, DC metro weekend campers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Shawnee and Susquehannock ancestral lands. Rich Appalachian mountain logging and conservation history.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Refreshing mountain stream energy, serene hemlock forest solitude.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Rushing river gorge, hemlock groves, rocky bluffs

public_reviews_summary: Top free primitive camping spot in Western Maryland. Cool mountain elevation, pristine Savage River trout water, and solid cell internet near Frostburg.
other_data: Maryland DNR State Forest. Free primitive camping.

name: Janes Island State Park Backcountry Water Trail Campsites

management_agency.name: Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) - Park Service

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - Free DNR Backcountry Water Trail Camping Permit required online (zero cost)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Primitive paddle-in coastal camping permitted at designated backcountry sites on Janes Island along Chesapeake Bay water trails.

nomad_connectivity_rating.overall_rating: Strong / Chesapeake Bay Open Water Tower Line

amenities: Chesapeake Bay Pristine Island Salt Marsh Campsites
